SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__smartlink2: Smartlink Level II: called shot +2 (not +4), a rangefinder −1 long / −2 extreme, a linked launcher −1, with a Level II receptor and smartgun, FoF pp. 84–85 and errata (book) or none (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__smartGoggl: Smart goggles: worn goggles tick their −1 row for a smartgun, and only one receptor counts beside a smartlink, Core p. 90 (book) or by hand, both adding (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__skillwires: Skillwires limit the total rating of all activesofts running at once, Core p. 249 (book) or each soft capped alone (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__softReplac: A running skillsoft replaces the character's own skill (its rating only); no magic skills on softs, Core p. 248 (book) or the better of the two (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__skillMemor: Skill Memory Table: headware memory a knowsoft or linguasoft takes by skill type and rating, Core p. 248 (book) or rating × Mp per rating (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__linedCoat: Lined coat: +2 Concealability for every weapon under a worn lined coat (looking and frisking), Core p. 242 (book) or no change (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__manualSear: Frisks: the Manual Detection Modifiers Table (professionalism, time, the searcher's state; a GM's strip search finds every weapon), NAGRL p. 93 (book) or none (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__sniffer: Chemical sniffer: one test, base TN 10 lowered by the ammunition and explosives carried, NAGRL p. 93 (book) or a test per explosive item (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__policeChec: Police check: the officer's Security or Police Procedures vs the Legality Rating (the GM's tool), Shadowtech p. 103 (book) or none (v980)
SR2E.HouseRules.Rule.KIT_V99__policeTn__: Police check: restriction number of an item needing a permit with no Legality code (VERIFY: 6)
Police check: restriction number of a restricted item with no Legality code (VERIFY: 4)
Police check: restriction number of a forbidden item with no Legality code (VERIFY: 2)
SR2E.Tools.kit99.label: Police check (book rules, GM)
SR2E.Tools.kit99.hint: The officer's Security or Police Procedures test against the Legality Rating of what a character carries (Shadowtech p. 103), rolled on your client and whispered to the GMs.
SR2E.Kit99.sl2Note: Smartlink Level II (receptor and smartgun both Level II).
SR2E.Kit99.oneReceptor: Smart goggles not counted beside the smartlink (one receptor).
SR2E.Kit99.UI.smartgun2Hint: A Level II smartgun system (Fields of Fire p. 57): with a Level II smartlink or smart goggles it gives the Smartlink II benefits.
SR2E.Kit99.UI.scopeHint: The Skill Memory Table's skill type (Core p. 248): how much headware memory the soft takes.
SR2E.Kit99.UI.legalCodeHint: The book's Legality code, e.g. 6P-CC (Shadowtech p. 103): its number is the police check's target number.
SR2E.Kit99.Search.strip: Strip search (6–10 minutes): every weapon found
SR2E.Kit99.Search.hint: The frisk rows are the Manual Detection Modifiers Table (Neo-Anarchist's Guide p. 93); only a GM can order a strip search.
SR2E.Kit99.Police.title: Police check (Shadowtech p. 103)
SR2E.Kit99.Police.intro: The officer's Security or Police Procedures skill against each restricted item's Legality Rating (its number), ±3 for the area's enforcement (never below 2). No success: nothing noticed; one: a warning; more: the officer presses the issue (a permit or an arrest).
SR2E.Kit99.Police.subject: Character checked
SR2E.Kit99.Police.all: Everything they carry (the officer suspects it or found it), not only what is in plain sight
SR2E.Kit99.Police.off: The police check is off (house rules: KIT_V99.policeCheck).
SR2E.Kit99.Police.noOne: No one to check: put tokens on the scene or make player characters.
SR2E.Kit99.Police.head: Police check of {subject} by {officer} ({dice} dice, enforcement {enforcement}).
SR2E.Kit99.Police.press: presses the issue: a permit, or an arrest
SR2E.Kit99.Police.nothingShown: Nothing restricted in plain sight (tick "Everything they carry" if the officer suspects more).
SR2E.Kit99.Police.hint: What the character carries is read from their own items. A concealed item needs the officer's Perception Test (a search) first.
